name: Pichavaram Mangroves
degradationDrivers: Upstream damming on Vellar & Coleroon rivers reducing freshwater flushing
Siltation chokes in narrow tidal creeks preventing seawater circulation
Plastic pollution accumulation from intense boat tourism
restorationInitiatives: TN-SHORE Mission (Tamil Nadu Coastal Restoration Mission 2023–2028)
MSSRF Fishbone Canalization Design (30° feeder canals restoring tidal flow)
Green Tamil Nadu Mission student sapling nurseries
Cuddalore Mangrove Conservation Centre establishment
description: Pichavaram Mangrove is one of India's largest estuarine mangrove systems, situated between the Vellar and Coleroon River estuaries. It features an intricate network of 4,400 small waterways, mudflats, and islets.

name: Muthupet Mangroves
protectionStatus: Part of Point Calimere Ramsar Complex (Site No. 1210)
degradationDrivers: Hyper-salinity during dry summer months due to reduced Cauvery fresh water
Massive canopy damage during Severe Cyclonic Storm Gaja (Nov 2018)
Lagoon bed shallow siltation restricting mangrove propagule dispersal
restorationInitiatives: MISHTI Scheme (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes)
MSSRF Community-based Village Mangrove Councils (VMCs)
Fishbone channel desiltation drives
CAMPA fund mangrove afforestation
description: Muthupet Mangrove Wetland forms the southern portion of the Cauvery river delta on the Palk Strait. It is characterized by extensive shallow tidal lagoons dominated by salt-tolerant Avicennia marina mangroves.

name: Point Calimere / Kodiyakkarai
degradationDrivers: Invasion of Prosopis juliflora (Seemai Karuvelam) choking mangrove mudflats
Historical salt pan expansion altering coastal lagoon hydrology
Feral cattle overgrazing on young Avicennia saplings
restorationInitiatives: Ramsar Management Plan for Site #1210
Prosopis juliflora invasive weed eradication drives
Tamil Nadu Forest Department Eco-Restoration Project
Migratory Bird Habitat & Bio-Shield Protection
description: Point Calimere Wildlife and Bird Sanctuary is a high-biodiversity coastal wetland complex comprising mangrove fringes, salt marshes, intertidal mudflats, and dry evergreen forest buffers.

name: Punnakayal Mangroves
protectionStatus: Forest Dept Fishbone Restoration Zone / Green TN Mission
degradationDrivers: Severe soil hypersalinity choking estuarine mudflats during low freshwater runoff
Encroachment from coastal salt pan operations
Industrial effluent discharge pressures near Thoothukudi port limits
restorationInitiatives: TN-SHORE & NABARD Funded Fishbone Canalization
Green Tamil Nadu Mission coastal bio-shield planting
Re-introduction of Rhizophora mucronata in low-salinity estuarine pockets
Prosopis weed removal across river mouth
description: Punnakayal mangrove forest is situated at the Thamirabarani river estuary. It undergoes active restoration using fishbone canalization techniques to enhance tidal flushing and coastal bio-shield protection.

name: Kazhuveli Wetland Sanctuary
protectionStatus: Ramsar Site No. 3026 / TN 16th Bird Sanctuary (2021)
degradationDrivers: Agricultural pesticide runoff from surrounding agrarian catchments
Coastal sand mining along Uppukalli creek entrance
Historical mangrove wood harvesting prior to sanctuary notification
restorationInitiatives: TN 16th Bird Sanctuary Protection Declaration (2021)
Designation as Ramsar Site No. 3026 (2024)
Mangrove bio-shield restoration along Edayanthittu estuary
Central Asian Flyway migratory bird conservation
description: Kazhuveli is the second-largest brackish water lagoon in Peninsular India, connected to the Bay of Bengal via Uppukalli creek. It features mangrove restoration patches protecting against tidal swash.

name: Pulicat / Pazhaverkadu Mangroves
degradationDrivers: Siltation of lagoon mouth mouth reducing seawater exchange
Thermal power plant fly ash and industrial effluent discharge
Erosion of outer barrier island dunes exposing mangroves to high wave energy
restorationInitiatives: MISHTI Scheme Mangrove Afforestation
Pulicat Bird Sanctuary Habitat Management Plan
Barrier island dune stabilization & mangrove bio-shield expansion
Community fishing welfare & eco-tourism regulation
description: Pulicat Lagoon is India's second largest brackish lagoon system, featuring estuarine mangrove fringes and barrier islands providing essential nursery grounds for estuarine prawns and mullet.

name: Ramanathapuram Island Mangroves
degradationDrivers: Destructive bottom trawling near island coral reef margins
Marine heatwaves causing seagrass die-off and mangrove heat stress
Islet shoreline scours during monsoonal storm surges
restorationInitiatives: UNESCO Biosphere Reserve Conservation Protocol
GoMBRT Seagrass & Island Mangrove Bio-shield Restoration
Artificial reef deployment to attenuate wave energy
Dugong & Turtle conservation sanctuary management
description: The Ramanathapuram island sector of Gulf of Mannar encompasses island mangrove fringes (e.g. Kurusadai Island) surrounded by extensive seagrass beds and marine bio-shield formations.

name: Devipattinam / Palk Bay Mangrove Belt
protectionStatus: Green Tamil Nadu Mission Coastal Bio-Shield Zone
degradationDrivers: Monsoonal wave scours along unprotected Palk Bay shoreline
Historical conversion of coastal intertidal land into commercial salt pans
High evaporation rates increasing summer soil salinity
restorationInitiatives: TN-SHORE Mission Coastal Bio-Shield Belt Expansion
Green Tamil Nadu Mission community mangrove planting
Palk Bay Dugong Sanctuary & Mangrove Corridor Linkage
Fisherwomen SHG mangrove nursery development
description: Devipattinam coastal stretch along the Palk Bay comprises dense intertidal Avicennia mangrove bio-shields planted to mitigate storm surges and shoreline erosion.
